classification.difficultyReason: The supplied diagrams directly cue the one taught same-arc doubling/halving relation; reflex sectors are explicitly marked. Nine similar applications add practice rather than new conceptual demand.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Minor AOB alpha; circumference ACB55 standing on same arcAB.
spec.mathematics: Minor AOB alpha; circumference ACB55 standing on same arcAB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc AB. Thus $\alpha=2(55^\circ)=110^\circ$.

spec.description: AOB88 given, gammaACB subtends same arcAB.
spec.mathematics: AOB88 given, gammaACB subtends same arcAB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The circumference angle is half the central angle on the same arc, so $\gamma=\frac{88^\circ}{2}=44^\circ$.

spec.description: C95 lies on minorAB arc; requested reflex AOB on opposite majorarc explicitly drawn belowcentre.
spec.mathematics: C95 lies on minorAB arc; requested reflex AOB on opposite majorarc explicitly drawn belowcentre.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The $95^\circ$ angle at C stands on the major arc AB. The corresponding reflex angle at the centre is $\alpha=2(95^\circ)=190^\circ$.

spec.description: Reflex BOA200 shown left majorarc, C on complementary arc; gammaBCA.
spec.mathematics: Reflex BOA200 shown left majorarc, C on complementary arc; gammaBCA.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle at C stands on the major arc BA associated with the given $200^\circ$ central angle. Hence $\gamma=\frac{200^\circ}{2}=100^\circ$.

spec.description: Reflex JOM258 majorarc not containing K; thetaJKM.
spec.mathematics: Reflex JOM258 majorarc not containing K; thetaJKM.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle at K stands on the same major arc JM as the reflex central angle $258^\circ$. Therefore $\theta=\frac{258^\circ}{2}=129^\circ$.

spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The circumference angle on arc AB is half the central angle: $\alpha=\frac{80^\circ}{2}=40^\circ$.

spec.description: QOP60 given, betaQXP subtends same minorQP.
spec.mathematics: QOP60 given, betaQXP subtends same minorQP.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle at X is half the central angle QOP on the same arc QP, so $\beta=\frac{60^\circ}{2}=30^\circ$.

spec.description: LKJ50 given, requested minor central LOJ gamma on same arcLJ.
spec.mathematics: LKJ50 given, requested minor central LOJ gamma on same arcLJ.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The central angle on arc LJ is twice the circumference angle at K. Thus $\gamma=2(50^\circ)=100^\circ$.

spec.description: RTS12 degree external leader; thetaROS on same minorRS, all original chords/radii.
spec.mathematics: RTS12 degree external leader; thetaROS on same minorRS, all original chords/radii.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle at the centre on arc RS is twice the circumference angle RTS: $\theta=2(12^\circ)=24^\circ$.
